description: A built-in type such as int, double, boolean or char whose variable holds the value itself.
A type such as String whose variable holds a pointer to an object, or null when it points to nothing.
Local variable type inference: the compiler deduces a fixed type from the initializer.
A modifier that allows a variable to be assigned exactly once.
An explicit conversion such as (int) value that narrows a type and may drop information.
The silent wrap-around that happens when an integer result does not fit its type.
A string literal delimited by three double quotes that keeps line breaks and strips common indentation.
